anomalies.obs: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the PWM driver U18 (PCA9685PW) has its address pin A0 (pin 1) strapped to +3.3V while A1–A5 (pins 2,3,4,23,24) are tied to GND, and the sheet note reads "I2C address: 0x41". U18 sits on the same I2C bus as the INA219 (SCL=NET0018, SDA=NET0095).
anomalies.expected: The design specification's component table states the PWM/servo driver is "NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40", i.e. A0 should be tied low (GND) so the device answers at 0x40.

evidence.quote: FCC Peripherals sheet, U18 PCA9685PW: pin 1 A0 -> +3.3V, pins 2/3/4/23/24 A1..A5 -> GND; note "I2C address: 0x41"; SCL pin26=NET0018, SDA pin27=NET0095
PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: The servo/PWM driver responds at I2C address 0x41 instead of the documented 0x40. Firmware built against the specified 0x40 will not communicate with the PCA9685, so no PWM/servo outputs are produced (the board behaves differently from the intended design).

parsed.summary: The schematic otherwise matches the specification (correct parts, the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap, 10 mΩ shunt, 5 V buck, 3.3 V LDO, sensor addresses), but the PCA9685 PWM driver's A0 strap and "I2C address: 0x41" note deviate from the spec's stated 0x40, which would leave the servo driver unreachable to firmware expecting 0x40.
